analyst_view.overall: PEC Zwolle (11th, 15 points) host AZ (4th, 26 points) on Sunday afternoon. PEC have a new coach, Alex Pastoor, who won his debut 3-1 at Telstar with a realistic, at times defensive approach (38% possession, five defenders late on); Gilles van der Wal missed that game (one report), and the brief's Krastev, Rahajaän and Floranus were not mentioned in what I read. AZ under Lee-Roy Echteld came from 0-2 down to win 4-2 at Sparta Prague on Thursday night, with substitutes Daal, Oufkir and Kwakman turning it, so they have a return trip and three days' rest before this game, which the numbers don't count. Striker Mexx Meerdink and defender Elijah Dijkstra stayed home as a precaution and were due back in the group on Friday (NOS via a news aggregator, Alkmaarsdagblad calls Meerdink injured); the numbers treat both as out until late December, so they may be taking too much off AZ's attack. Marc Nagtegaal's low card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and take 15% off AZ's goals for Meerdink, their top scorer, plus smaller cuts for Smit, Schouten and Hornkamp. Meerdink stayed home from Prague as a precaution and may be back in the squad, which would mean the numbers took off too much, but AZ also played a draining away game on Thursday night and Pastoor's PEC set up cautiously; these pull both ways, so I stay at about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, 5.9 for AZ, and already count PEC's 34 corners in six and AZ conceding few. Pastoor's more cautious approach might cost PEC some corners, but one game is too little to read, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards and already take about 15% off for Marc Nagtegaal, who shows about 2.7 a game. No cards or flashpoints were reported from AZ's game in Prague and both sides' bookings are close to normal, so I stay at about 2.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add 11% to AZ for 100 shots in their last six. AZ played away in Prague on Thursday night and come into this with tired legs, and PEC under Pastoor kept the ball only 38% of the time in his first game, so I lean mildly lower, to about 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target, most of them AZ's (5.9). The Thursday trip points slightly lower, while a possible Meerdink return pulls the other way, so I trim only a little, to about 9.3.
